body.estimand_functional: Identified critical inference functional: \(\widehat\tau=(-\widehat a_T-\nabla\widehat\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\), with \(\sqrt{n/L_n}(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))\Rightarrow N(0,V(P))\), consistently estimated covariance \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^R\), simultaneous fixed-grid ellipses, and squared risk of order \(L_n/n\) under \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/7\).

sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the order-\(s\) signed periodized KDE followed by clipping at \(c/2\) and mass renormalization. The maintained polynomial window is \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/7\). The half-open-cell lift selector returns the two map translations and potentials with a fixed measurable fallback off its regular domain. Covariance pilots are two-fold cross-fitted, retain harmonic and generated-target components, and are evaluated by adjoint elliptic solves; \(n^{-1}I_{2J}\) is added before block inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) only when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).
Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere boundary problem.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual law and map under cyclic comonotonicity, while the estimation section gives consistency rather than a sampling law.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify the gradient-Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the abstract reports numerical stable-type fluctuations but the paper does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.
Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound.
Theorem 18 gives the \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth density plug-in map without a matching logarithmic lower bound.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient influence functions and root-\(n\) cross-fitted inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data.

body.tldr: The note proves intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes identification, the translation-aware four-input derivative, and a uniform energy-parametrix analysis of the two-dimensional critical plane. The specified positive-normalized periodized-KDE and nested Monge--Ampere plug-in has a fixed-grid Gaussian limit at \(\sqrt{n/L_n}\), the full four-cell Green covariance is consistently estimated by cross-fitted adjoint solves, the multiplier ellipses have simultaneous coverage, and the \(L_n/n\) squared-risk order is matched by Green-aligned Hellinger-local alternatives.

project_justification.gap: Published transport central-limit results cover the critical two-dimensional point-gradient limit only in the fixed-source uniform-law case, while fixed-path differentiability does not control shrinking-bandwidth empirical directions or generated targets. The proof here closes that gap with a uniform energy parametrix, transformed-coordinate convolution bounds, moving-pole control, and a mixed-norm nested linearization.
project_justification.niche: In the critical plane, each independent cell contributes a positive logarithmic Green variance. Nesting makes both control cells enter through a common leading outer response and leaves an order-minus-two generated-target remainder; after the exact Jacobian-density cancellations, each control contribution has weight \(\alpha(y_j)\), while each treated contribution has weight one.
project_justification.fill: The note delivers the identified translation-aware displacement, its full variable-coefficient four-cell covariance, a class-uniform fixed-grid Gaussian approximation, feasible cross-fitted adjoint covariance estimation, simultaneous bivariate multiplier ellipses, and matching class-uniform upper and fixed-center Hellinger-local lower squared-risk bounds under the sharp mixed-remainder window \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/7\).

body.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC supplies the Euclidean proper-convex-support multivariate changes-in-changes identification and consistency motivation; the present note proves a separate intrinsic full-support flat-torus identification result. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the uniform-to-uniform fixed-source critical limit and supplies the one-map mixed linearization template, but not generic coefficients, four varying cells, or a generated target. GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supplies fixed smooth-path one-map differentiation. The new arguments are the energy-parametrix covariance calculation, its transformed-kernel and moving-pole stability, the explicit two-stage mixed tame expansion, and their use for feasible nested inference and matching local risk.
body.interpretation: At each prespecified treated-post location \(y_j\), the causal estimand is the translation-aware no-treatment displacement \(y_j-T(y_j)\), identified from the four observed laws by cyclic comonotonicity. Its covariance block is \(w_j\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}H(y_j)/(4\pi f_{T1}(y_j))\), where \(w_j=\alpha(y_j)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})+\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\). The simultaneous ellipses preserve direction and local covariance of every bivariate arrow while controlling multiplicity over the fixed grid.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The theorem is fixed-grid and assumes four independent smooth samples on the flat torus, uniform density positivity, uniform Brenier ellipticity, a fixed lift/cut-locus margin, fixed \(J\), and \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/7\). It does not assert finite-bandwidth block diagonality or zero harmonic translations: the implementation retains all such score terms before covariance formation. Numerical Monge--Ampere and adjoint solves must approximate maps, coefficients, poles, and score covariances below their statistical scales.
body.honest_scope: The proved results concern a balanced four-cell repeated-cross-section experiment with fixed \(J\), smooth positive periodic densities, and translation-aware torus displacements. They do not provide a continuum confidence band, allow vanishing densities or degenerating Jacobians, or justify applying the method directly to raw discrete or paired Card--Krueger outcomes. A Card--Krueger reanalysis requires a prespecified smooth bivariate periodic outcome construction, a defensible independent-cell sampling approximation, and numerical tolerances below the critical scales.
